subject: Morning Analyst Inbox — 2026-11-06
body:
Morning Analyst Inbox — 2026-11-06

Cutoff: 07:25 São Paulo / 10:25 UTC. Book prioritization is provisional: portfolio weights remain a seed. These are research priorities, not trade instructions.

Today's focus: AMZN for an internal model contradiction; IREN for funding scope and delayed delivery; ABNB/BKNG for divergent travel execution; NET for monetization versus cash conversion; STX for pricing durability.

Evidence key: E = _wiki/_meta/analyst-evidence/2026-11-06-morning-source-checks.json. “supp-” IDs are supplemental research signals, not engine-generated alerts.

FIVE PRIORITY IDEAS

1. AMZN — Challenge our own AWS margin before debating the Street.

Evidence: Capstone's October 30 AWS cash-cost study, ingested November 5, puts CY27 AWS margin at 41.4–43.5%, versus 46.2% in the model it reviewed. The difference is cash costs: 32.7–34.8% of revenue in the study versus a hard-coded 30% in model row L202. The study itself estimates a $7–13bn EBIT gap; these are its scenarios, not new estimates or management guidance. Its revenue-growth input is still an aggressive +48%.

Inference/action: a revenue bull case does not automatically justify a cost bull case. Ask the model owner to reconcile power/O&M growth, utilization, lease/D&A treatment and Bedrock gross/net accounting. The study also has limits: historical cost elasticity may not hold at its assumed growth rate. Do not mechanically replace one assumption with another.
Falsifier: a documented cost bridge supports the model's 30% cash-cost ratio without inconsistent accounting or unsupported operating leverage.
Signal supp-20261106-amzn. Evidence: E.amzn; _wiki/AMZN.md; relatórios bons/AWS_Cash_Costs_Estudo_2026-10-30.html. All four archived study pages visually checked.

2. IREN → CRWV/MSFT — Funded deployment is not a funded company.

Hard evidence: IREN's November 5 release moves its >$4bn operational ARR target from year-end to January, potentially end-February. “Fully funded” is conditional and applies to the supporting 0.3GW IT program. Wider expansion still seeks $6bn of funding. Contracted prepayments and undrawn facilities are not cash already received. [Company release](https://iren.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/iren-reports-q1-fy27-results)

Number conflict: GS / Michael Ng and team, November 6, calls $200m “AI Cloud Services” revenue. The release splits that total into $135m services and $65m leases. Reconcile forecast scope before accepting the claimed revenue beat. Bernstein / Gautam Chhugani and team, November 6, emphasizes prepayments and owned power; neither removes commissioning risk.

Inference/action: request a project-by-project unrestricted-cash, draw-condition and acceptance bridge. Do not assign the aggregate delay to Microsoft's unnamed delayed supplier.
Falsifier: further commissioning slips or unmet financing conditions prevent the targeted ramp.
Signal supp-20261106-iren. Evidence: E.iren; _wiki/themes/ai-compute-deals.md, existing IREN-MSFT-202511. No standalone IREN wiki page.

3. ABNB/BKNG — Test execution and booking timing before blaming travel demand.

Hard evidence: Airbnb's November 5 release reports nights and seats +16% and revenue +19%; every region delivered double-digit nights growth. This challenges a blanket travel-demand slowdown explanation for Booking's Q4 room-night guide of +1–3% (BKNG company, November 3). [Airbnb release](https://news.airbnb.com/airbnb-q3-2026-financial-results)

Broker evidence: JPM / Doug Anmuth, Dae K Lee and Margaret Hoffman, November 6, attributes 3pp of Airbnb's nights growth to Reserve Now, Pay Later. It raises its target $170→$202 but stays Neutral.

Inference/action: compare European accommodation bookings on matched stay dates, excluding seats and adjusting for longer booking lead times, cancellations and promotional timing. Product improvements could be taking share, but these headline growth rates do not prove it.
Falsifier: the divergence disappears after those adjustments, or forward bookings fail to become completed stays.
Signal supp-20261106-travel. Evidence: E.travel; _wiki/BKNG.md, November 5 peer-read-through block. No standalone ABNB wiki page.

4. NET — Consumption monetization is arriving; cash conversion still needs scrutiny.

Hard evidence: Cloudflare's November 5 release reports $782.5m revenue, +39%, and Q4 guidance of $845–846m. Non-GAAP gross margin is 72.4%; FCF margin is 10%, versus 13% a year ago. Exact FY26 revenue guidance is $2.963–2.964bn, not an unqualified $3bn. [Company release](https://www.cloudflare.com/press/press-releases/2026/cloudflare-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results/)

Broker evidence: JPM / Samik Chatterjee, Jaiden Patel and Mashu Nishi, November 6, reports NRR of 122%, variable consumption approaching mid-teens of revenue, and initial OpenAI-related Act IV revenue.

Inference/action: upgrade the monetization evidence, not every long-term assumption. Request the split between recurring commitments, variable overages and initial Act IV receipts; bridge growth to network capex and cash returns. Initial revenue is not proof of material scale.
Falsifier: consumption growth fades without durable commitments, or gross-profit and cash generation fail to follow revenue.
Signal supp-20261106-net. Evidence: E.net; _wiki/NET.md.

5. STX — A real meeting readout closes the information gap, not the 2028 pricing debate.

Broker-relayed evidence: MS / Erik Woodring, Dylan Liu, Maya Neuman and Rauf Ural, November 6, reports a three-day roadshow with CFO Gianluca Romano and IR Shanye Hudson. Management says CY27 volumes and pricing are negotiated; CY28/29 exabytes are committed, but pricing remains to be negotiated. It reports no HAMR qualification problem and expects December volume acceleration.

Inference/action: test pricing protection, cost pass-through and cancellation rights. MS's CY28 EPS of $89.21 and large buyback scenario remain analyst forecasts—not contracted earnings or company guidance. The wiki's October 29 filing analysis also warns that tax/accrual timing boosted cash flow.
Falsifier: December exabyte acceleration fails, or component inflation and customer renegotiations undermine margins.
Signal supp-20261106-stx. Evidence: E.stx; _wiki/STX.md; _wiki/_meta/outcomes.md. Yesterday's “no readout” assessment is superseded.

MODEL CONTROLS AND NARRATIVE

Standing controls, not fresh alpha: GOOG's June 5 house revenue versus November 5 BBG remains a gross/net mismatch (esti-08489ebe8988). CRWV's October 14 house EPS losses of -$3.27/-$1.83 for CY26/27 are smaller than BBG November 5's -$3.95/-$2.25: the house is more optimistic, despite the engine's “below” label (esti-da5fddd49d94; esti-8faeb5b5943c). LITE's June 16 $12.81 versus BBG November 5 $15.22 needs vintage/basis reconciliation (esti-3b370f174b10). Evidence: E.model_controls; _wiki/_data/house.json; _wiki/_data/estimates.json.

Additional conflict: MS's November 6 STX note says gross debt $2.8bn; the wiki's company-filing record has $2.383bn at September and approximately $1.63bn after October redemption. Reconcile dates/basis before using MS's capital-return argument. Signal supp-20261106-stx; E.stx.

Narrative: distinguish demand, delivery and funding. GS / Michael Ng and team, November 6, frames Texas risk as delayed service dates and higher costs, not necessarily cancellations. This is broker analysis, not verification of a blanket enacted moratorium. Signal supp-20261106-calendar; E.narrative.

CATALYST PREPARATION

• Today, November 6, 1pm ET: Jefferies / Julien Dumoulin-Smith's Texas policy webinar, per November 5 invitation; no replay. Prepare questions on grandfathering, already-energized sites and permitting authority. No registration performed.
• November 10, CRWV: 5pm ET results call, per its October 27 [company notice](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Announces-Date-of-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-and-Conference-Call/default.aspx). Prepare parent liquidity versus restricted/project cash and deployment-acceptance questions.
• DDOG follow-up: the November 5 JPM CEO/CFO NDR invitation promises a replay. No dedicated readout found in this morning's subject inventory/selected excerpts; obtain it before treating renewal-pricing concerns as resolved.
Signals supp-20261106-calendar and esti-8faeb5b5943c. Evidence: E.calendar; _wiki/CRWV.md; _wiki/DDOG.md.

WHAT CHANGED VERSUS YESTERDAY

New priorities: the newly ingested AWS model conflict; IREN's delivery/funding and revenue-basis disclosures; Airbnb's stronger counterexample to OTA weakness; NET's acceleration; and STX's actual meeting readout. COHR contract protection, FICO mortgage pricing and DDOG renewal economics remain open—not invalidated by dropping out of today's top five.

Engine: 37 active / 1 high / 29 focus names, versus yesterday's emailed 40 / 1 / 32. The later November 5 rebuilt file was 48 / 3 / 38: four belief alerts rolled off, four source-date catalyst items were reclassified, and three missing-readout items were logged as unresolved. Those reductions are not bullish resolutions. Zero automated belief changes does not mean zero new evidence. Evidence: E.engine_delta; _wiki/_data/analyst/history/.

Scope: 905 mailbox entries inventoried; selected research bodies and primary/local evidence reviewed, not an exhaustive audit. Outcomes and the compute-deal timeline were updated; company pages and house models were not edited.

delivery.normalization: Whitespace/numbered-list escaping and connector-inserted semicolons after O&M and D&A; no substantive differences.

coverage.scope: All fixed-window subjects inventoried; selected message excerpts reviewed. Not an exhaustive report or filings audit. Own automation messages not independent evidence.

maintenance.outcomes: NET and ABNB operating bull; IREN mixed; STX readout supersedes prior missing status, future tests open.
maintenance.compute_timeline: IREN-MSFT-202511 partial delivery; conditional program funding and delay; unnamed contracts unmapped, no new totals.
